subject: general
question: Which of the following materials is used as a binding agent in organic brake linings?
solution:
The correct answer is __Resin**(Option 1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Resin__ is commonly used as a binding agent in organic brake linings.
 
• Organic brake linings are made from materials such as rubber, carbon, and other fibers, which are bound together using resin.
 
• Resins provide durability, heat resistance, and binding strength to the brake linings.
 
• They ensure the brake linings adhere properly to the brake system and withstand the friction generated during braking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Metal Powder:**

 
 
• Metal powder is primarily used in metallic brake linings and not organic ones.
 
• It helps in enhancing the thermal conductivity and strength of metallic brake pads.
 
 
 
• **Rubber:**
 
 
• Rubber is used as a component in organic brake linings to provide flexibility and noise reduction.
 
• It is typically combined with resin to improve binding properties.
 
 
 
• **Cotton:**
 
 
• Cotton fibers are occasionally used as fillers in brake linings but are not the primary binding agent.
 
• They provide additional strength and structure to the material.
